reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A group of three disorders affecting creatine synthesis or transport: AGAT (GATM) deficiency, GAMT deficiency, and the X-linked creatine transporter (SLC6A8) defect
The two synthesis defects are autosomal recessive, whereas the creatine transporter defect is X-linked and chiefly affects males
All three share a marked reduction of the cerebral creatine peak on brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy, a key diagnostic clue
Common clinical features are intellectual disability, speech delay, epilepsy and behavioural or autistic features
GAMT deficiency is distinguished by accumulation of the neurotoxic intermediate guanidinoacetate and can cause a movement disorder and refractory seizures
The synthesis defects (AGAT and GAMT) are treatable with oral creatine supplementation, with additional dietary and pharmacological measures in GAMT to lower guanidinoacetate
The creatine transporter defect responds poorly to supplementation because the transporter needed for brain uptake is defective
Urine and plasma creatine, guanidinoacetate and the creatinine metabolite ratio help distinguish the three subtypes
reference.pathophysiology: Creatine and its phosphorylated form provide a rapid energy buffer for tissues with high and fluctuating energy demands, notably brain and muscle. Creatine is synthesised in two steps: AGAT (encoded by GATM) forms guanidinoacetate, which GAMT then methylates to creatine; creatine is delivered to the brain and taken up by cells via the SLC6A8 transporter. Loss of any step causes cerebral creatine depletion and impaired energy homeostasis, producing neurodevelopmental impairment. In GAMT deficiency, guanidinoacetate additionally accumulates and is neurotoxic, contributing to seizures and movement disturbance. In the transporter defect, creatine is made normally but cannot enter the brain.
additionalDifferentials: Non-specific intellectual disability of other genetic causes
Autism spectrum disorder without an identified metabolic cause
Fragile X syndrome and other X-linked intellectual disability syndromes
Primary movement disorders (particularly in GAMT deficiency)
additionalInvestigations: Brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrating a reduced or absent creatine peak
Plasma and urine guanidinoacetate (raised in GAMT, low in AGAT deficiency)
Urine creatine-to-creatinine ratio (raised in the transporter defect)
Molecular genetic testing of GATM, GAMT and SLC6A8
A monitored trial of creatine supplementation with repeat spectroscopy in synthesis defects
redFlags: Global developmental delay with epilepsy and prominent speech impairment
Refractory seizures and a movement disorder suggesting GAMT deficiency
Regression or deterioration during intercurrent illness
Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance in males
reference.prognosis: Outcomes in the treatable synthesis defects (AGAT and GAMT) are substantially improved by early creatine supplementation, and pre-symptomatic treatment can prevent much of the neurological damage. The X-linked creatine transporter defect has a less favourable prognosis because supplementation does not restore brain creatine.
pitfalls: Overlooking a treatable cause of intellectual disability by not requesting spectroscopy or guanidinoacetate testing
Assuming all creatine deficiency syndromes respond to supplementation, when the transporter defect does not
Missing raised guanidinoacetate as a marker of the treatable GAMT form
Delaying treatment in synthesis defects, when early therapy is most effective
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Oral creatine monohydrate supplementation is the mainstay for the synthesis defects (AGAT and GAMT), replenishing depleted cerebral creatine
In GAMT deficiency, additionally lower neurotoxic guanidinoacetate through dietary arginine restriction and ornithine supplementation
Institute treatment early, ideally pre-symptomatically, to prevent neurological damage
Antiepileptic therapy for seizures, particularly the refractory epilepsy of GAMT deficiency
Developmental support with speech and language therapy and behavioural and educational interventions
For the X-linked creatine transporter (SLC6A8) defect, provide supportive care, as creatine supplementation is largely ineffective and precursor trials show limited benefit
Monitor response with repeat brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy and biochemical markers
Genetic counselling and family screening, autosomal recessive for the synthesis defects and X-linked for the transporter defect, including carrier and newborn testing
